publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: Conference proceedings front matter may contain various advertisements, welcome messages, committee or program information, and other miscellaneous conference information. This may in some cases also include the cover art, table of contents, copyright statements, title-page or half title-pages, blank pages, venue maps or other general information relating to the conference that was part of the original conference proceedings.

articleTitle: "A Modified Delta-Sigxa Quantizer To Obtain High Resolution A/D Conversion With Small Excess Sample Rates"
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: There are a number of techniques [1] which use a combination of excess sample rate and signal processing to obtain enhanced resolution analog-to-digital conversion (ADC) from a reduced resolution quantizer. The common thread in these techniques is the formation of correlated data by sampling and quantizing a bandlinited signal at a rate considerably above its Nyquist rate. Coherent signal processing of these correlated samples improves the signal to quantizing noise ratio by the processing gain (ie., the ratio of coherent gain to incoherent gain) of the processing. This improvement in signal to noise ratio (SNR) is viewed as the conversion of excess sample rate to additional bits of quantization. Feedback and spectral noise shaping improves the rate at which we can exchange the excess sample ratio for improved resolution. One system which successfully ap- plies both techniques is the delta-sigma modulator. This paper presents a number of modifications to the standard delta-sigma configuration which permits high resolution conversion while operating at small excess sample ratios.

articleTitle: A Diffusion Based Edge Detector/sup 1/
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: In this paper we are concerned with the parallel implementation of step edge detector optimal under Canny's optirnality. We show that optimal IIR filter can be derived from diffusion networks. Thus these filters lead to very efficient parallel implementation both as analog combinatorial circuits and as switched capacitors circuits.

articleTitle: Estimation Of Parameters Of Point Objects In 2D Sampled Images
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: Using 2-D sampled fields of view generated by scanning or staring arrays of detectors, the velocity of unresolved point objects (UFO) is usually derived from position estimates in a series of two or more successive 2-D fields, or "frames". A recursive linearized maximum-liklihood estimator used for position and intensity estimation, and which can be shown to achieve the Cramer-Rao bound, is described and extended to the single-frame estimation of velocity. Estimator precision is exhibited fo r object velocity in the neighborhood of 1/10 detector subtense/detector integration time. Estimator Precision is demonstrated by Monte Carlo methods based on simulation of the estimation process.

articleTitle: A Multiprocessor System For Real-time Implementation Of Spatial Domain Digital Filters
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: This paper presents an efficient multiprocessor system for real-time implementation of spatial domain digital filters. This multiprocessor system uses a specially designed digital signal processor (DSP) as a node and operates asynchronously without requirement for global synchronization between DSPs. It is based upon an efficient algorithm decomposition technique which minimizes data communication requirements between DSPs without increasing computational complexity. A very high order spatial domain digital filter can be implemented by cascading lower order sections with the total number of the processors increasing only at a linear rate. This multipro- cessor system is an implementation of a wavefront array processor for spatial domain filters.

articleTitle: An Exact Programmable Switched-capacitor Equalizer
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: A digitally programmable switched-capacitor equalization filter is presented. The design is entirely carried on the z-domain, which leads to exact transfer functions. The filter uses a structurally all pass section as a basic building block, resulting in a robust equalizer with low sensitivities with respect to capacitor ratios. Experimental results obtained with a discrete prototype are included.

articleTitle: A Synthetic Neural Chip
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: A compact synthetic neural cell that is compatible with CMOS technology is described. Some issues related to its applications are discussed. Particular emphasis is placed on training algorithms and connectivity.

articleTitle: Gaussian Convolution Analog CMOS Network For 2D Images
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: The design of an analog CMOS LSI is presented, that contains a matrix of photoreceptors and a network of posi- tive and negative resistors, capable of performing a 2D Gaussian convolution on a 6Ox6O sampled image in less than 2@is. Details of circuits in a conventional 2/spl mu/m CMOS technology are given, along with simulated performance.

articleTitle: Multiply Replicated Arrays For Direction Of Arrival Estimation
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: In this paper, we consider a new multi-sensor array structure and algorithms for direction of arrival estimation for multiple narrow-band sources. The proposed array is composed of many identical sub-arrays with known fixed displacement and zero rotation relative to one another. Physically, the array may be constructed from a number of multiplets (uniform linear arrays), all having the same inter-sensor spacing and orientation. The locations of the individual multiplets can be arbitrary and unknown. The sensors on the same multiplet must be identical, but sensors on different multiplets may be different. The choice of multiplet length presents a trade-off between robustness to perturbations and resolution performance. We study this trade-off through simulations.

articleTitle: Nearly Optimal, SVD-Based Stacking Of Seismic Data
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: Given several realizations of a time, sequence corrupted by white noise, it is desired to estimate the noise-free time sequence. The simplest method is to form an equally weighted average of all the realizations. A second method which is commonly employed in the geophysical industry and provides reasonable performance at low signal to noise ratio (SNR) is to normalize each input time sequence to the same power level. These approaches are generally not optimal, but the signal strength and SNR information necessary for optimal weighting is usually not known. We propose a recursive algorithm utilizing principle component analysis which has near optimal performance at output SNR's greater than 0 dB. The algorithm also provides a usable estimator of output SNR. Simulations and comparisons with other weighting approaches are included.

articleTitle: Lp Normed Spectral Estimation Residual Analysis
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: Seismic sonic log data is characterized by a relatively high signal-to-noise ratio with the possible presence of one or more impulses arising from the data acquisition environment. Frequently, in order to completely analyze sonic log data, a high resolution frequency estimation technique is required that is resistant to the possible presence of impulsive noise. Previous work has shown that increased frequency resolution is possible fo r multiple sinusoids contaminated by impulsive noise utilizing an L1 normed solution to a set of linear prediction equations. In an actual data analysis scenario, however, the interpreter is uncertain whether impulsive noise is present. This paper outlines how the complex kurtosis of the residual vector may be conveniently used as a test statistic for deciding if impulsive noise is present and consequently to decide whether to incur the additional computational expense of calculating an L1 normed solution.

articleTitle: Solid Modelling Data Structures For Computer Vision
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: The data structures and access mechanisms used in representing objects in computer vision have generally been of little interest. While a conceptual description of the information in a symbolic scene representation is frequently described, the actual underlying structures for this representation are normally ignored. As more parallel approaches are applied to the scene Model generation task, this becomes less adequate. In an environment typified by multiple, competing models being modified by several processes, it is necessary to pay more attention to the question of maintaining a consistent model structure. In addition, the careful development of a general purpose scene modelling environment provides the ability to pay more attention to issues in the vision task, and less to symbolic representational issues. This paper describes a solid modelling environment for computer vision. The modelling system implements a hierarchical object structure, with points, lines, polygons, rigid objects, and articulated objects. User programs are able to freely manipulate these entities, without concern for the underlying representations. Model manipulation is defined in terms of graph grammar productions.

articleTitle: Switch-Box Routing Based on Corner-Edge
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: Taking a 2-terminal switch-box subject to no knocked-knee rule, a routing algorithm, or rather a principle, CORNER-EDGE is proposed. it classifies a given connection requirement set into N/sub tb/, N/sub lc/, the nets connecting the opposite sides vertically and horizontally, and the rest N/sub k/. CORNER-EDGE realizes the nets of N/sub k/ first, optimally in a sense. Then, it picks up certain nets, called the top nets, from N/sub tb/ N/sub lr/ and route them alternatively, and repeat. A reasoning why such a strategy is adopted is described.

articleTitle: Non-classical Fault Detection In Dynamic CMOS
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: Due to increased complexity, testing and fault detecting have acquired lot of importance in modern VLSI technology. CMOS and specially dynamic CMOS logic families are widely used in present day VLSI circuits. This paper focuses on one such family called the Domino Logic and analyses the issue of fault detection. Instead of studying the conventional stuck at faults, it investigates the nonclassical stuck open and stuck on faults. Stuck on faults in the Domino circuit are harder to detect and additional transistors may be used to alleviate the difficulty.

articleTitle: Effect Of Correlation On Signal Detection In Arctic Under-lee Noise
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: Signal detection in a large segment of nonGaussian and non-stationary Arctic under-ice noise, which contains both high power narrow-band and impulsive components, is examined. It is shown that the correlation functions of sub-segments of data change significantly, and if ignored, can degrade the performance of a detector. For a false alarm probability of 0.05 and a known constant signal, the matched filter was on average 17.6% better than a detector designed assuming independent noise sam- ples. It is also shown that pre-processing the data with an adaptive notch filter, then us4ig the matched filter will result in a further improvement of about 6%. Additionally, the effect two different signal shapes have on the performance of the matched filter is examined.

articleTitle: An Overview Of Design Methods For Sensor And Actuator Error Identification And Adaptive State Estimation
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: In this paper we overview a number of methods for the identification of control system sensor and actuator errors and for correct plant state estimation for feedback control when such errors are present. The methods viewed deal with additive and multiplicative (gain change) sensor and actuator errors. Additive sensor and actuator errors are first considered for both single- input, and multiple-output plants. The computational methods described are highly relevant to practical situations. Next, multiplicative sensor and actuator errors are considered and new methods for error identification and state estimation for these situations are demonstrated. This approach applies to plants with multiple actuators and multiple sensors, and can be combined with additive error methods. An original, constructive state variable inverse filter design technique is viewed and used to compute arbitrary actuator errors and their effects on the plant state. Then, the use of inverse filtering in combination with the methods for accomodating a multiplicative sensor errors is investigated.

articleTitle: RAM-JET: Towards The Removal Of Multiplicative Compleidty In Digital Signal Processingvlst Arclutectures
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: The concept of a programmable systolic cell is introduced that allows finite ring arithmetic to be performed using bit-level systolic arrays. The motivation for this work is the recent introduction of a fixed coefficient bit-level inner product step processor operating over a finite ring (BIPSPm). From design and fabrication experiments performed on this cell, it is clear that it represents a major step forward in the implementation of very high speed fine-grained DSP algorithms. The remarkable properties of the cell are the ability to implement fixed product multiplication with only twice the area overhead of a bit-level binary adder, and yet provide operation at slightly higher throughput rates. The cell also has low overhead associated with error detection, and an entire array of an arbitrary number of cells in a linear pipeline, can be tested with only 32 test vectors in the time taken to pass the vectors through the array. This paper discusses a programmable system that will operate with a modified cell, to allow arbitrary algorithms to be implemented without incurring the overhead associated with general multiplication. Rather than seek algorithms that minimize multiplication, we can rather seek algorithms that provide a homogeneous VLSI structure.

articleTitle: Feature-based Motion Analysis
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: A sequence of images of a dynamic scene m provide information about the structure of objects in the scene and about the motion of the objects or the observer. Two general classes of techniques have been applied to this problem called long- range and short-range methods. These are primarily distinguished by the distance between corresponding points in consecutive frames. This paper compares short-range and long- range techniques in general terms. The paper also presents results from a general feature based motion analysis system.

articleTitle: Knowledge-based Interpretation Of Bioelectrical Signals: Examples In EEG Analysis
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: A system is described for the automated interpretation of bioelectricif signals. A knowledge-based approach is taken. providing two separate, cooperating knowledge bases, one for the signal analysis knowledge and one for the more subjective interpretation knowledge. Examples of the performance of a system similar to that described are given in the area of EEG analysis.

articleTitle: Traveltime Tomography And Nonlinear Constrained Optimization
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: Fermat's principle of least traveltime states that first arrivals follow ray paths with the smallest overall traveltime from the point of transmission to the point of reception. This principle determines a definite convex set of feasible slowness models - depending only on the traveltime data - for the fully nonlinear traveltime inversion problem. The existence of such a convex set allows us to transform the inversion problem into a nonlinear constrained optimization problem. Fermat's principle also shows that the standard undamped least-squares solution to the inversion problem always produces a slowness model with many ray paths having traveltime shorter than the measured traveltirne (an impossibility even if the trial ray paths are not the true ray paths). In a damped least-squares inversion, the damping parameter may be varied to allow efficient location of a slowness model on the feasibility boundary.

articleTitle: A Fast Multi-valued Sbnr Multiplier
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: A novel multi-valued SBNR Multiplier architecture using redundant numbers in the encoded partial product generators is described. The architecture employs an efficient blend of voltage- mode and current-mode cells in an attempt to overcome the deficiencies of each mode employed separately. Our methodology capitalizes on the salient properties of multi-valued and binary techniques within a systems context. A brief review of VLSI techniques for multi-valued lo IC implementations is provided, including CDIOS, I L, ECL, TSL, and STL. Advantages and disadvantages of each technology are given as well, with a focus on multi-valued logic (MVL) applications.

articleTitle: Functional VLSI Design For Low Level Image Processing ICs
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: We propose a VLSI circuit design method which is derived from a functional decomposition of low level image processing algorithms. In order to design high powerful architecture, we have been testing this functional approach quite extensively and special purpose circuits have already been developed. Finally from a broad class of various image processing algorithms and operators, we have defined a computational unit called functional element. These elements is to be associated in order to form a mesh connected programmable data flow computer. This data flow computer had been defined in order to get a straight mapping of the expressed algorithms thanks to the functionnal programming proposed by BACKUS. Thus, high computing power can be easily obtained for real time complex image processing applications. Using the equivalent data flow graphs of the algorithms, this computer can help to determine whether a given combination of precisely specified IC operators would have the requested behaviour, so that special purpose VLSI could be easily designed. In this paper the approach will be described shortly as well as the programmable data flow computer we defined. Several examples of implementation onto this computer are shown in order to point out the salient concept and advantages of this approach.

articleTitle: Signal Processing Methods For Inverse Problems In Electrophysiology
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: Estimation of bioelectric source potentials using remote electric field measurements is known as the inverse problem in electrophysiology. Both numerical and analytic approaches to this problem have been developed, analytic solutions having the advantage of explicit parameterization in terms of measurable tissue properties. This paper describes an analytic Fourier Transform method for determining frog sciatic nerve activity from limb surface potential measurements. The thigh is modeled as a cylinder containing one bioelectric source (the sciatic nerve) and a major inhomogeneity (the bone). Idealized electrical properties are assigned to the limb tissues. A forward solution predicting surface potentials resulting from sciatic nerve activity is derived, and re-expressed as the action of a 2D filter, representing the thigh, on source potentials. Inversion of the forward filter provides an ideal inverse solution, which is modified in the spatial frequency domain to eliminate excessive sensitivity to noise. Predicted and measured sciatic nerve potentials are compared, and various modifications to the idea filter are examined.

articleTitle: Distributions For Seismic Signal Representation
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: This paper describes an application of distributions (e.g. spectrograms) to the interpretation of continuous data streams from seismic array stations. Such data representations can be used to construct an analyst in- terface for the purpose of screening large quantities of data. Three types of distributions are considered: spectrograms (energy vs. frequency and time), bearing and slowness distributions (energy vs. direction or slowness and time). The main seismic interpretation functions of detection, wave identification and association, location, and event classification can be performed from a visual inspection of an appropriate combination of distributions and trace displays. A system based on data "visualization" should have high throughput and perform well in a nuclear test ban treaty verification role. "Work performed under the auspices of the U.S. Department of Energy by the Lawrence Livermore Na tional Laboratory under contract number W-7405-ENG- 48."

articleTitle: A Vision Recognition System For High Accuracy Position Control For Laser Reconfigurable Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: The machine vision algorithms required to increase the accuracy of a manipulator to that of its resolution are presented. This high accuracy is required for laser pro- gramming of reconfigurable integrated circuits. An ap- plication specific integrated circuit has been fabricated that performs the time-criticad aspects of the image recognition algorithms at video rates.

articleTitle: Adaptive Arma Lattice Based On Generalized Mullis-roberts Criterion
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: In this paper, an adaptive algorithm is presented for an ARMA digital lattice filter, whose parameters are estimated based on a formulation using generalized Mullis-Roberts criterion. The ARMA digital lattice filter is obtained directly from independent AR and MA prediction error recursion formulas which evolve from a parameter estimation algorithm based on the generalized criterion. The adaptive lattice algorithm is based on the well known LMS method of error minimization. Experimental results obtained from applying this adaptive algorithm to several system identification type modeling problems are shown.

articleTitle: Motion Analysis From Three-dimensional Profiles And The Applications
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: The development of motion estimation has been an important topic in machine vision research. In this paper, we assume 3-D data acquisition capability and concentrate our analysis on the algorithm structure. For simplicity, we classify various versions of the algorithms based on the availability of the constraints such as object rigidity, point features, and matching correspondences. In addition to the analysis of the algorithms at various levels, one of the purposes of this paper is to describe the modifications and fundamental changes of the algorithm structure corresponding to the stages of the constraint availability.

articleTitle: Image Recognition By Human Decision Makers
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: New technology permits the design of systems which project a human essence into regions that are incompatible with his corporeal presence. On the basis of received optical images the operator acts in a situation assessment and resource allocation role. This paper provides the results of a study of an analytical model of human response for tasks of this type. Simulation and an empirical study using a representative test subject confirm the behavioral properties of the model.

articleTitle: A Limited Sensing Random Access Algorithm With Binary Success-failure Feedback
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: We consider the problem of Random Access Communication over a time slotted channel, with binary Success/Failure feedback. The feedback informs the users only whether or not there was a success (single transmission) in the previous slot. For the above problem we propose and analyze a limited feedback sensing algorithrn (each user is required to observe the channel feedback, from the time he generates a packet to the time that this packet is successfully transmitted). The limit Poisson user model is adopted. The algorithm achieves a throughput of 0.322 and it induces low delays for relatively low input rates.

articleTitle: On Combining Decentralized Reduced Order Estimates*
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: A method is present which allows one to fuse local reduced order estimates into one global reduced order estimate.

articleTitle: Generalized Processor-Memory Bandwidth Analysis For Fully Shared-Memory Multiprocessors
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: Effective bandwidths of crossbar and multiple bus interconnections applied for shared-memory multiprocessors are analyzed. The analysis uses general access patterns among processors and memories. Band- width functions of the interconnections are mathematically proven in creasing with respect to the number of buses and memory access rates. The minimum bandwidth is obtained when uniform access is assumed, and the maximum when memory references are concentrated to one memory module for each processor. Even if some of the access probabilities are given fixed, the minimum and maximum are similarly found when the remaining access probabilities are equal and concentrated, respectively.

articleTitle: An Efficient Method In The Design Of 2-D Recursive Digital Filters For Communication Systems
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: This paper presents an optimal design approach of 2-D recursive digital filters on the basis of symmetry. After studying, a method used to guarantee the stability of the 2-D recursive digital filters that make the complex checking of the stability be more simplified, Nth-order coefficient matrix ge- neral formulas being directly used to design are derived. Filter design example is included.

articleTitle: Analog VLSI For Early Vision Processes
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: Real time image understanding systems are required for many applications. However, early vision processes are "ill-posed" problems, these problems require extensive computational resources and thus limit the performance and speed of machine vision systems. It has been recently proposed that these problems can be solved using resistive networks. We are in the process of designing VLSI circuits which will perform edge detection and estimation of the motion field.

articleTitle: Polynomial Multiplication And Filter Design Via Fourier Transforms
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: The convolution property of the Fourier Transform is used for solving the problem of substituting one polynomial into another, as with the BLT (bilinear transform). Using transform techniques, first a BLT is computed and then a bandpass filter is designed using the substitution s=/spl alpha/(z/sup 2/-2/spl alpha//spl beta/z + 1)/(z/sup 2/ - 1_, where /spl alpha/ and /spl beta/ are real numbers that are determined by the passband.

articleTitle: Technology Trend To Manufacture Future VLSI Systems
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: This paper highlights the multi- technology processes, specifically both BiCM0S technologies and EEPROM combined with digital/analog technologies are addressed. Some additional information on the design of EEPROM (Electrically Erasable Programmable ROM) cells and its applications in the digital and analog areas are also discussed.

articleTitle: Window Shaping In The Design Of FIR Filters
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers

articleTitle: A Topological Global Routing Algorithm For General Cells
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: An algorithm is presented to accomplish the global routing for general cell routing problems. More specifically, the branch-and-bound method is used to find the minimal cost path that is feasible between two pins on the routing surface. An extension of this algorithm is used to form multipoint nets. The algorithm is described and illustrated.

articleTitle: An Electronic Vision System For Sorting Cotton Boll Worm Pupae By Sex
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: The cotton boll worm Heliothis zea and the tobacco bud worm Heliothis virescens are becoming increasingly resistant to pyrethroid based insecticides. Rather than using more powerful chemicals to control these pests, an environmentally safe biological control system is being developed. This system, based on the mass release of sterile male insects, requires the sorting of large quantities of boll worm pupae by sex. This paper describes the specification and design of a computer vision system developed for this task. The system presented represents a transfer of technology from the military to the agricultural sector as it employs multiple sensors, feature extraction techniques, and performance measurement criteria initially developed for military computer vision systems.

articleTitle: BLR: The Bus-line Router
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: A now routing algorithm based on the principle of the 'bus-line router' design is presented. The algorithm has the advantages of both maze-router and channel router that are small routing areas, high routibility, and high routing speed. The switch box problem is avoided. The basic approaches of the algorithm are using minimum bus lines to get small routing areas, and choosing the optimal distribution of terminals to increase the probability of the success of close routing. Both close routing and open routing methods are described. The complete CAD layout package, which includes layout input, global router, and detail router by using the bus-line router algorithm, has been implemented in C, on SUN workstation at San Jose State University.

articleTitle: Broadband Matched Field Processing
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: The analysis here will illustrate the use of full wavefield (matched field) processing techniques in a multipath environment. Experimental data consists of the arrivals at a, hydrophone array from an explosive source in shallow water. A coherent recombination of the multipath arrivals is performed in order to provide enhanced signal-to-noise ratio for source detection as well as range/depth localization.

articleTitle: A Graph-theoretic Approach For One-dimensional Logic Gate Assignment Of Vlsi Circuit Layout
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: This paper proposes a new approach for the one-dimensional gate assignment problem. By converting the original problem to a graph G, we transform the gate assignment as a qraph-theoretic problem. A minimum-cut algorithm is applied to the graph G to find the node- ordering which corresponds to the gate assignment in the original problem. This new approach is shown through comparison with published examples to produce optimal solutions.

articleTitle: Dynamic Control Of Time-domain Analysis In The Spice-pac Simulation Package
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: SPICE-PAC is a circuit simulation package which is upward compatible with the popular SPICE-2G6 simulation program. Although SPICE-PAC constitutes the "core" of several interactive simulators, the best use of its flexibility is in "integrated" software tools in which circuit simulation is combined with other software tools for circuit optimization, device parameter fitting, multi-level simulations, etc. Recently the package has been subjected to a series of modifications required by "enhanced cir cuit simulation", i.e., computer-aided circuit analysis that allows users to extend, modify and replace some of the "standard" sim- ulation capabilities. This paper describes modifications which provide "external" run-time control of time-domain (transient) analysis, and shows simple applications of this mechanism.

articleTitle: New Directions In DSP From Texas Instruments
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: This paper describes what Texas Instruments is doing to provide further advances in the three areas of market direction. The paper details how the company has, in the past, made advancements and suggests some future ideas under consideration. Please note that the future ideas, discussed in this paper, are speculative in nature and therefore none of these ideas should be construed as a plan to develop or offer any product or service by Texas Instruments. The future ideas sections are in italics. Please interpret these accordingly.

articleTitle: Past Iteration Algorithm For Optical Flow Computation
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: In this paper, we propose the successive over-relaxation (SOR) method to speed up the optical flow computation. We derive a linear algebraic system having a large sparse matrix from the elliptic partial differential equations by finite different method. Using the successive over-relaxation (SOR) method, the system can be solved by gaining speed factor of at least two over other algorithms. Comparing to the conjugated gradient (CG) method, this method requires local neighbour connections only for each iteration without involving the whole large matrix interaction and it takes much less computation time for each iteration. Therefore the SOR method is more efficient.

articleTitle: Maximum Likelihood, Weighted Kalman And Subspace Linear Prediction Algorithms For System Identification
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: For the problem of estimating parameters of a linear system from its input and output sequences, we present iterative quadratic maximum likelihood (IQML), iterative quadratic weighted Kalman (IQWK), and noniterative subspace linear prediction (SLP) algorithms. The SLP algorithms are based on a novel subspace deconvolution of the output. In particular, a double total-least-squares (D-TLS) SLP algorithm is provided.

articleTitle: System Applications Of A New 32-Bit Floating-point DSP Processor
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: Embodiment of DSP tasks requires an optimal blend of reg- ularly structured array processing and scalar oriented decisions making. The ZR34325 represents the first full IEEE floating- point integrated array processor on silicon, supplemented with the pertinent scalar and control flow capabilities. In order to meet the stringent processing requirements, found today in modern signal and image processing applications, the ZR34325 directly executes embedded DSP and array processing primitives on multidiniensional arrays. Furthermore, an integrated development environment which includes system software simulator, vectorized and parametric DSP, arithmetic and matrix library, C based assembler/linker and hardware development tools, facilitates top-down complete application development . To achieve performance bounds higher than plausible by a single device (45 MFLOPs peak), one must resort to a Multi- Processor Multi-Tasking (MPMT) schemes. The ZR34325 en- ables very efficient MPMT schemes for tasks where: (i) Execution- time is data independent (e.g. FFT); or (ii) Execution-time is data dependent (e.g. SVD algorithm).

articleTitle: An Adaptive IIR Lattice Filtering Algorithm
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: A new approach to solving the adaptive ITR lattice filtering problem is presented here. In this approach, correlation ( or secondary ) data are used to estimate the parameters of the unknown filter. As a result, the filtering algorithm derived will treat equation error model and output error model in the exactly same way; and the criterion function of this algorithm is always quadratic. By using a minimum- phase recursive multichannel AR process lattice estimator, a minimum-phase adaptive IIR lattice filtering algorithm can be readily realized.

articleTitle: An Ode Approach For Analyzing The Tracking Behavior /spl dagger/ Of Adaptive Algorithms
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: In this paper, a general framework for studying the mean tracking behavior of adaptive algorithms is examined. The Ordinary Differential Equation (ODE) approach used in the context of stationary signals is extended to the tracking of non-stationary signals. By using weak convergence theory and the pre-scaling technique, it is shown that an ODE can be used to study the mean behavior of the algorithm. Some applications are considered to demonstrate the applicability of the theory. Computer simulations are also provided to sub- stantiate the analysis.

articleTitle: Minimal-order Feedback Control Design
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: In microprocessor-based control, it is often important to develop control strategies using retatively low-order controllers in order to trade computational Load for higher control rates. This paper gives new results for minimal-order observer- controller design computations for plants with both muttiple-inputs and multiple-outputs. In a number of cases, lower-order digital controllers are obtained than with existing methods.

articleTitle: A 3-D Texture Model Of Natural Scene Image
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: A new 3-D texture model is developed by considering scene image as the superposition of a random texture image and a smooth shaded image. This smoothed surface is obtained by taking average of pixel intensities from natural image, and texture image can be generated by substracting the smoothed image from the original one. Then, Shape from-shading technique is applied to estimate the orientation of surface. For describing a random texture image, the long-correlation periodic model is chosen because of its good performance in texture synthesis and its ability to represent the coarseness and the pattern of the surface at the same time. Then, a projection technique is developed to deal with this particular random model, which has a non-isotropically distributed texture pattern. For estimating the parameters, a hybrid method which uses both the least square and the maximum likelihood estimates is applied directly to the given intensity function.

articleTitle: Biomagnetic Imaging: A View From Fourier Space
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: Biomagnetic imaging is the estimation of electrical activity patterns in humans and animals from measurements of the magnetic fields this electrical activity generates. We concentrate our attention here on the mathematical procedures used to form these estimates. In particular, Fourier transforms will be used extensively to provide intuitive descriptions of these procedures. We present a very abbreviated history of biomagnetic imaging followed by descriptions of magnetic field generation. We show how Fourier transforms can be used to develop a transfer function description of imaging system properties as well as simplifying reconstruction algorithms. Finally, the problem of magnetic field extrapolation from limited sets of measurements is discussed and a Fourier transform based solution is presented.

articleTitle: Image Reconstruction Using The Bispectrum*
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: The resolution of a standard telescope imaging system is severely limited by temperature-gradient induced phase fluctuations in the atmosphere. Short exposure images, however, during which the atmosphere is effectively frozen, contain diffraction-limited resolution information about the object. Techniques for extracting this information are collectively called "speckle interferometry". He will show that by averaging the complex bispectra of an ensemble of images, the Fourier phase of the object can be estimated. This estimate, combined with a standard estimate of the Fourier magnitude using the average power spectrum, will then yield a diffraction-limited reconstruction of the object. We also present results of a simulation of this technique, which demonstrates the reconstruction of an extended, noisy object from a series of short exposure images.

articleTitle: A Parallel, Non-parametric, Non-iteratrve Clustering Algorithm With Application To Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: This paper describes a parallel, non-parametric, non-iterative clustering algorithm with application to segmentation of textured/ color/multispectral images. It groups multidimensional features extracted from the image into distinct clusters. Segmentation is done by mapping back these clusters into the spatial domain. The process starts with generation of a feature vector histogram in the multidimensional space. A parallel hillclimbing procedure is then utilized to identify local peaks which correspond to the center of clusters. Each peak must pass a cluster validity test or get merged with another nearby peak. Application of this technique to textured images is presented. The textural features extracted from local regions in the image are six estimated parameters of random field models fitted to the region and two other local statistics namely: sample mean and variance (total of eight features). The implementation of the algorithm on a SEQUENT S81 MIMD parallel processor is discussed.

articleTitle: L/spl infin/ Theory Based Computer Aided Controller Synthesis for Time-Delay Systems
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: This paper reports a result on the method of computer aided feedback controller design for possibly unstable time-delay systems. The design objective is to reduce the weighted sensitivity. It is shown that the proposed design method is in an asymptotical sense L/spl infin/ optimal. The resulting controller is either of neutral delay type, or of retarded delay type.

articleTitle: 2-D Constrained Harmonic Retrieval*
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: For a two-dimensional harmonic signal that consists of p plane waves, it is well known that the covariance matrix will be a rank p Hermitian Toeplitz block Toeplitz matrix. When the covariance matrix is estimated from the data, however, the covariance ma, trix will not generally satisfy these constraints. Therefore, in this paper an iterative algorithm is presented that serves as a prepro- cessor for incorporating the rank p and Tbeplitz block Toeplitz constraints on the measured covariance matrix. Examples are given to demonstrate the improvement that the algorithm provides in estimating the frequencies of the harmonic signals.

articleTitle: Adaptive Filters For Digital AGC As Applied To Abnormal Holter ECG
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: Adaptive coefficient IIR filters are considered for determining the digital gain for AGC applied to Holter ECG data. The filter coefficients are adapted using the actual and filtered QRS complex peaks. The normal and abnormal data tapes were used to validate the algorithm. Compared to fixed coefficient filters, the adaptive filters are shown to produce bias free digital gain and avoid the possibility of missing normal beats in a fixed threshold QRS complex detector.

articleTitle: Intensity Dependent Spread Filters
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: We propose an extremely efficient, approach for the implementation of an intensity dependent filter which models the operation of the human retina. Such filters are required in photographic and electronic imaging applications. The derivative properties of B- spline functions lead to orders of magnitude reduction in both the number of arithmetic operations and circuit complexity.

articleTitle: Filters With Small Non-linearities
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: The Kalman filter provides a finite dimensional solution when the signal and observation processes are linear and have Gaussian noise. In this paper the effect of a small non- linearity in the signal is discussed by considering stochastic flows for the signal and a Girsanov transformation for the observation. The result can be expressed in terms of Gaus- sian densities.

articleTitle: Split-Levinson-type Algorithms For LS Linear-phase Filtering And Fbpm Prediction/sup 1/
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: In this paper, the correspondence between the efficient Split-Levinson algorithm and linear-phase filtering is exploited. Least-squares estimation subject to a linear-phase constraint leads to a persynnnetric sample covariance matrix in the normal equations. We introduce a new orthogonal- ization scheme for the data vectors. This scheme is appropriate for problems with the structure of a liticar-phase constraint. The symmetric linear-phase prediction polynomials effecting this orthogonaligmtion procedure obey a thrcetemn recursion, as in the Split-Levinson algorithin, with the addition of an extra term involving the Kalman gain. As a byproduct, the predictor polynoinial of the Forward-Backward Prediction Method (FBPM) can be recovered from the linear-pliase polynomial, paralleling a similar relationship in the Split-Levinson algorithm. Finally, we also describe how the batch-processing fast LS algorithm can be converted into a time-recursive solution. This yields a fast lattice algorithin for solving the corresponding RLS problems. The multichannel prewindowing formulation is considered.

articleTitle: A Very High-speed FFT Device Architecture
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers

articleTitle: Gamma Spike Circumvention Algorithm - Performance Analysis
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: Theoretical analysis on performance of an analog clamping gamma spike circumvention algorithm is presented. The analysis includes relationships among the key parameters such as the bandwidth of circuit, threshold value, and gamma flux. Especially, the effect on signal power loss due to blanking by the circumvention circuit is analyzed with respect to the gamma and Gaussian electronics noises. The result can be used to find optimal conditions on the circuit design as well as operation parameters, so that it can be served as a tradeoff tool for algorithm selection and development.

articleTitle: A Fast Least Square Deconvolution Algorithm For Vocal Tract Cross Section Estimation
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: An efficient computation algorithm, based on unitary Jacobi-type rotations, is developed in this paper for fast least square deconvolution. Specifically, this algorithm is able to solve a positive definite covariance matrix with a special Toeplitz structure in O(N /sup 2/) operations instead of O(N3) operations. Taking advantage of the inherent structure of the underlying deconvolution problem, this algorithm is guaranteed to be numericall.y stable since only unitary transformation is used. It has been implemented on an experimental human vocal tract cross section estimation system. Significant gain in processing speed has been observed.

articleTitle: Least Squared Error FIR Filter Design Using Spline Transition Functions
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: This paper proposes that the use of transition functions and transition bands of the ideal amplitude frequency response allows the analytical design of optimal least squared error linear phase FIR lowpass digital filters with an explicit control of the transition band edges. This is in contrast to the use of window functions which only implicitly control the transition band edges and which destroy the optimality of the approximation.

articleTitle: Sampling Rate Alteration In Circulator Wave Digital Filters
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: The study, presented in this paper indicates that the computation rate is minimized in two- or three- stage realization. Based upon this conclusion a simple method is presented to design the optimum convertor using circulator wave digital filters. A coefficient optimization scheme for multistage realization is presented.

articleTitle: A Prime-factor Decomposed Algorithm For The Discrete Sine Transform
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: A fast computational algorithm is presented for the discrete sine transform. The algorithm is based on the so-called prime- factor decomposition approach for the size of the transform N which is a product of two relatively prime factors N /sub 1/ and N/sub 2/. The equations obtained in the derivation am used to provide the input and output index mappings. Mapping tables can be constructed and the computational complexity is also briefly discussed.

articleTitle: A Hierarchical Data Structure To Support Diagnostic Testing
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: The diagnostic testing of large integrated circuits is described using an electron-beam prober to measure internal waveforms. The design data of a specimen is displayed to guide interactive testing. Further, this design data is organized as a hierarchy of symbolic objects, to facilitate the extraction of circuit models. In particular, connected structures are maintained as entities, making it easier to generate simulated waveforms rapidly for comparison with measurements from designated nodes in the device. An implementation of the data structure is presented, in Ada, which was developed under contract for the US Army, Fort Monmouth, NJ.

articleTitle: Efficient Implementation Of Chirp Z-Transform Using A Cordic Processor*
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: In this paper, an efficient implementation of the Chirp Z Transform (CZT) using a CORDIC (Coordinate Rotation Dlgital Computer) Processor is presented. The proposed implementation is most effective when only a very few complex frequencies on the Z -plane is to be evaluated via CZT. In particular, it is shown that a seal- ing operation in the CZT algorithm can be conveniently implemented with a norm correction (normalization) computation, which is often considered as an overhead, in the CORDIC algorithm. Furthermore, since the desired frequencies of CZT are specified before computation, it is possible to reduce the total number of CORDIC iterations by finding a most economic representation of the angle in terms of the elementary CORDIC rotation angles. A greedy algorithm which takes only O(n2) operations is developed to perform the angle recoding. Simulation results are also presented to verify the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: An Efficient Routing System For Block Layqut
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: A flexible and powerfid routing system for arbitrarily sized blocks is presented. Through the years various algorithms have been proposed for individual phases of the routing process (channel slicing global routing, compaction, etc.). This paper describes a complete set of algorithms which solve the problems commonly encountered during different stages of block routing. Some of the features that set this apart from previously published work are: 1) A channel generator that breaks placement cycles and guarantees slicing; 2) An intelligent global router that considers routing congestion and wiring length trade-offs; 3) Density estimation and compaction modules that operate during the routing; 4) A single-pass design-rule driven gridless router that handles irregularly shaped channels. These modules combine to form a fast and efficient block routing system.

articleTitle: Segmentation Via Multiple Looks Of Image Sequences Using The A Priori Probability Mask
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: A multiple-look segmentation technique for processing image sequences which uses a probability mask is presented. By designing the segmentation process in two stages; the probability mask formation, and the refinement by the Maximum A Posteriori(MAP) decision rule, a more reliable silhouette of a moving object is obtained for classification. Experimental results are presented showing the a priori probability mask formation and a comparison of the results of the Maximum Likelihood(ML) decision rule with those of the MAP decision rule. Here we assume that geometry(or shape) does not change within the "window" of looks required to perform the segmentation.

articleTitle: Optical Interconnects
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: The performance of advanced multiprocessor architectures of the future will be governed by the bandwidth and configuration of the communication channels between various subcomponents of the overall system. Optics and optoelectronics have an important role to play in alleviating the communication bottleneck in these systems. This paper will describe the current and planned developments of optical interconnection.

articleTitle: Applications Of The Martin Marietta Single Module Advanced Systolic Array Processor
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: An overview of the Martin Marietta Advanced Systolic Array Processor (ASAP/sup TM/ ) will be presented. The modular design of the ASAP allows a user to build as large a processor as desired by concatenating multiple, independently programmable unit arrays. Each unit array, housed on a single VME card, is composed of a two- dimensional grid of 256 bit serial nearest-neighbor con- nected processors (SINID), a local controller, and all I/O support. Multiple unit arrays can be configured in any configuration desired; that is all SIMD, groups of SIMD arrays with MIMD between groups, or all MIMD. As an example, mapping of a conventional digital time-delay-and- sum beamformer algorithm onto a massively parallel ASAP array will be illustrated,

articleTitle: A Summary Of Estimation In Electrical Machine Systems
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: With increasing regularity, estimation algorithms are be- coming prominent components of electrical machine sys- tems. Their capabilities contribute significantly to improved system performance. In summarizing these contributions, this paper outlines the contemporary role of estimation in high-perfomance electrical machine systems and provides several examples related to motion estimation. Additionally, this paper looks forward, ontlining potential uses of estimation in electrical machine systems, and directions for continued research.

articleTitle: Soft Constrained LMS Algorithms: A Robust Procedure For Signal Misalignment
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: This paper presents a new algorithm for both broad- band and narrowband adaptive bearnforming which is robust to both desired signal misalignment and array imperfections. By utilizing available a priori information, the new algorithm minimizes desired signal cancellation by introducing new soft constraints which are incorporated into the LMS adaptation algorithm.

articleTitle: Optical Flow From Real Images
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: In this paper a new method which computes the optical flow from a sequence of time-varying images is presented. The use of second order derivatives of the image brightness provides a solution to the aperture problem. Experimental results on sequences of real images, together with estimates of 3D motion parameters, like time-to-crash for translation and angular velocity for rotation, are presented and discussed. Due to the remarkable accuracy which can be achieved in estimating motion parameters, the proposed method is likely to be very useful in a number of computer vision applications.

articleTitle: The Use Of Decentralized Control On The Vibration Supression In Large Flexible Dynamic Systems
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: In the present paper the problem of vibration suppression in large flexible dynamic systems is considered. The decentralized control law discussed is based on model reference adaptive control theory. Conditions for global stability are derived based on stability properties of the local subsystems and the coupling among them.

articleTitle: Autoregressive Modeling Of Dispersive Microstrip Tansmission Lines
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: Microwave and high-speed VLSI integrated circuits are lirnited by the propagation characteristics of the on-chip in- terconnections. Pulse dispersion on microstrip transmission lines is simulated using an equivalent lumped-distributed circuit. Transient analysis circuit simulations are performed to generate a synthetic time domain response. The impulse response of the simulated microstrip line is determined and modeled by an autoregressive lattice filter. The microstrip measurement technique will use photoconductors with picosecond pulsing and sampling speeds. The photo- conductors are excited by a pulsed laser and picosecond time domain measurements are obtained along the microstrip. Computer simulation results are compared with available measurement data to evaluate the performance of the model.

articleTitle: Enhanced Performance Single-chip DSP Requires Minimal External Circuitry
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: The ADSP-2101 is a 16-bit single-chip digital signal processing (DSP) microcomputer. The goals in designing the ADSP-2101 were to minimize external hardware and the accompanying extraneous logic while maintaining a high performance parallel architecture.

articleTitle: Reduced Order Kalman Filtering Of Moving Images
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: This paper presents some preliminary results on the application of the extended Kalman filter to the reduction of noise in moving images. A large savings in the number of computations required is obtained by implementing the filter in the spatial frequency domain. The resulting filter is shown to be composed of fourth order filter segments, in parallel, followed by an FIR filter. In addition to the computational savings, this architecture is well suited to implementation using systolic array technology.

articleTitle: Shape From Shading In Sar Imagery: Experimental Results
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: In this paper experimental results are presented for the estimation of topography from the radiornetric, or shading, information in SAR imagery. This can be thought of as a computer vision problem, viz. shape from shading (SFS). Because of the noise inherent in SAR imagery and the ill- posed nature of the SFS problem, an iterative solution is used which allows for noise and incorporates a regularization term in the cost function. Two practical issues are recognized. First, unknown reflectance model parameters must be estimated from the image data. Second, shading does not provide reliable information about the low frequency components of the surface. Both difficulties are reduced by utilizing auxiliary low resolution surface height information. This is demonstrated by combining SFS results from SIR-B SAR images with much lower resolution terrain elevation data to construct high resolution terrain elevation estimates.

articleTitle: Lower Bound Analysis For Large Errors In Nonlinear State Estimation
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of estimating a state vector from a sequence of data generated by a nonlinear process. In particular, the effects of nonlinearity on performance bounds for large estimation errors are analyzed via the marginal density function. The use of local processing to produce a reduced data set, under conditions of asymptotic normality, provides a simple mechanism for formulating a likelihood function. Nonlinear estimation techniques are then applied to a reduced order system (reduced dimensionality), and an approximation of the marginal density is obtained with the corresponding error bounds. This method of hierarchical processing results in both computational efficiency and algorithm flexibility. As an illustrative example, simulated results are presented involving noisy and biased data. Deviations from the linear assumptions inherent in the use of the traditional Fisher information matrix (FIM) are explained.

articleTitle: The Weitek 64-bit Floating-point Datapath Unit
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: The WTL 3164 and VVTL 3364, jointly referred to as the WTL 3X64 are each 64-bit floating-point datapath units designed for high-speed operation in pipelined environment while making possible full compliance with the IEEE standard for binary floating-point arithmetic, as well as full interruptibility, including in pipelined environment. This paper describes the architecture and performance of the 3X64.

articleTitle: Real Time Multiplication And Division For VLSI DSP
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: This paper describes recent developments in VSLI design for real-time digital signal processing. In particular, designs for integer multiplication for use in FIR, IIR and lattice filters and floating point division applicable to both adaptive filtering and standard deviation computations, will be talked about at length. Emphasis here is on the internal architectures of the arithmetic units not on their applications. The research presented in this paper has been proven reliable and feasible by completing the design, lay-out, and fabrication in silicon.

articleTitle: Adaptive Beamforming For Large Arrays
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: Adaptive and high-resolution array processing techniques are usually considered for relatively small arrays in which the number of snapshots is large compared to the number of array elements. In this paper we consider the case of a large array in which the number of snapshots is smaller than the number of sensors, and therefore the sample covariance matrix is rank deficient. A numerically stable adaptive beamforming algorithm is derived for this case, and it is shown how eigenstructure based algorithms such as MUSIC need to be modified to handle the case of large arrays.

articleTitle: Rendering Of Texture On 3D Surfaces
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: This paper presents a novel and computationally efficient model based algorithm for artificially rendering textures on a 3D surfaces. We use a Gaussian Markov Random Field (GMRF) for modelling the texture. The GMRF has been shown to faithfully reproduce a vast class of micro and macro image textures. Unlike other methods of textune rendering which are either iterative or subdivisional in nature, the method presented here uses just a Gaussian random number generator and FFT computations for rendering the textures. Moreover, no data interpolation is needed or used. As such, it is computationally simple, efficient, and fast. It relies on reflecting in the GMRF structure, the functional relationships that exist between the original homogeneous texture and the texture that results from either the "orthographic" or "perspective" distortions. The latter are functions of the surface type and shape. This method applies for any 3D analytic surfaces , or for more complex nonanalytic surfaces which are specified by an array of surface normal directions at different points on the surface.

articleTitle: Monotonic Search Networks For Computer Vision Databases
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: Design criteria for an associative network database for com- puter vision which supports monotonic search for the best match of an unknown entity are discussed. The network paradigm used provides for associative clustering of similar entities, and thus higher levels of abstraction are supported. A small database using thirty entities, each represented by a Fourier feature vector, is constructed and tested.

articleTitle: Numerical Properties Of Algorithm-Based Fault-Tolerance For High Reliability Array Processors *
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: Algorithm-Based Fault-Tolerance is a method of applying block error codes to array implementations of linear algebraic operations. When the underlying algebra is the real (or complex) number field, then numerical approximations to the reals cause certain fault-induced errors to be indistinguishable from roundoff errors, so that fault-induced errors may be either undetected or miscorrected. A worst case forward error analysis of floating-point implementations of minimum redundancy (SEC) codes shows that locating errors is inherently more difficult than detecting them. It is demonstrated that SEC Reed-Solomori (DFT) codes with equivalent theoretical power don't have equivalent numerical properties. A new minimum dynamic range SEC code is shown to be superior to all other minimum redundancy SEC codes. For integer affithmetic, the optimal method to add and to use available precision for encoding and decoding circuits is derived. Multiplierless SEC codes based on generalized Hamming codes and multi dimensional checksum codes are described.

articleTitle: Verifying The Accuracy Of Machine Vision Algorithms And Systems
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: The Purpose of this paper is threefold: (a) to summarize important parameters and procedures for verifying the measurement and recognition (classification) accuracy of machine vision algorithins/systems; (b) to alert the machine vision research community to the current, very inadequate practice in this important area; and (c) to propose some measures to improve this situation. Two example applications from our practice are given in order to illustrate experimental verification procedures we presented. The motivation for the paper is based on the fact that machine vision systems are very hard to model or simulate accurately, so realistic large scale experiments seem to be the only reliable means of assessing their accuracy. However, in the machine vision (research) community this veffication is seldomly done ade- quately. We feel that until this situation is improved, the transfer of research ideas into practice will be difficult.

articleTitle: Algorithms For The Segmentation Of Speckled Images
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: This paper presents new algorithms for the segmentation of speckled images, including synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images. These algorithms are based on a hierarchical random field model proposed for speckled images and maximum a posteriori (MAP) segmentation using simulated annealing. Different versions of the model are developed to represent single- or multi-look and intensity or complex speckled images. In an earlier study, a similar segmentation algorithm was presented for single-look intensity speckled images. The algorithms in this paper treat single- and multi-look complex speckled images and multi-look intensity speckled images. These algorithms constitute an extension and an improvement over the earlier one. Parameters of the speckle processes are estimated as part of the algorithm. The segmentation algorithms are implemented on a wide class of synthetically generated and actual speckled images. The results verify that significant improvement is obtained when multi-look and complex image data is used for the segmentation.

articleTitle: A New Breakthrough In Linear-system Theory: Kharitonov's Result
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: Given a real coefficient polynomial D(s), there exist several procedures for testing whether it is strictly Hurwitz (i.e., whether it has all its zeros in the open left-half plane). If the coefficients of D(s) are uncertain and belong to a known interval, such testing becomes more complicated because there is an infinitely large family of polynomials to which D(s) now belongs. It was shown by Kharitonov that in this case it is necessary and sufficient to test only four polynomials in order to know whether every polynomial in the family is strictly Hurwitz. An interpretation of this result in terms of reactance functions (i.e., LC impedances) was recently proposed. These results were also extended recently for the testing of positive real property of rational transfer functions with uncertain denominators. In this paper we review these results along with detailed proofs and discuss extensions to the discrete-time case.

articleTitle: Advances In Photodetector Arrays For Optical Processing
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: Recent advances in photodetector arrays for optical processing are reviewed with emphasis on two new unpublished developments. Discussed in detail is a 1024xi element CCD photodetector array that has a demonstrated performance of 56 dB (19 bits) optical power dynamic range; 8 microsecond frame readout time; a IE-16 J noise equivalent energy at 830 nm; - 48 dB lag; and low crosstalk. Performance and design issues are discussed with emphasis on issues that have not been widely discussed in prior literature. Such an issue is temporal lag which limits the performance of high throughput optical processing systems that employ time-integrating pholodiode arrays and charge-coupled devices. Finally, future prospects in photodetector arrays for optical processing are discussed.

articleTitle: Mathematical Morphology And Computer Vision
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: An algebraic system of operators, such as those of math- ematical morphology, is useful for computer vision because compositions of its operators can be formed which, when their meaningful parts and separate the meaningful parts from their extraneous parts. Such a system of operators and their compositions permit the underlying shapes to be identified and reconstructed as best possible from their distorted noisy forms. As well they permit each shape to be understood in terms of a decomposition, each entity of the decomposition being some suitably simple shape. Since shape is a prime carrier of information in machine vision, there should be little surprise about the importance of mathematical morphology. Morphological operations can simplify image data preserving their essential shape char acteristics and eliminate irrelevancies. As the identification and decomposition of objects, object features, object surface defects, and assembly defects correlate directly with shape, it is only natural that mathematical morphology has an essential structural role to play in machine vision.

articleTitle: The Architecture Of VLSI Digital Signal Processors
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: With the introduction of now VLSI techniques, new levels of integration were possible. These new techniques and higher levels of integration allow the implementation of optimized processors for specific applications with large requirements. Real-Time Digital Signal Processing (RT-DSP) was an area whose requirements were riot achievable by the technology that was available in the mid 1970's. Obviously, the requirements for RT-DSP depend on the application, but in the general case were large enough for most general purpose microprocessors, thus requiring the search for others cost-effective solutions. One of the proposed solutions was the use of specialized processors, highly optimized for digital signal processing tasks. These specialized processors, are often referred as digital signal processors. According to their degree of optimization, digital signal processors had been classified into several generations: first, second, third and possibly a fourth (next) generation. This document presents a survey of digital signal processors, together with a set Of expectations for next generation processors. This document represents an extract of some of the conclusions found in [1] in which a larger and more comprehensive survey and analysis of the optimizations performed in most digital signal processors as well as a set of recommendations, expectations andlor projections for next generation processors were presented.

articleTitle: A Computational Model Of Texture Segmentation
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: We present a. computational model of human texture segmentation and argue for its utility in machine vision. Major theories due to Julesz and Beck attribute preattentive texture segmentation to differences in first-order statistics of stimulus features such as orientation, size and brightness of constituent elements. An alternative approach seeks to exploit psychophysically observed spatial frequency channels and neurophysiologirally observed blob, bar- and edge-sensitive mechanisms, and perform simple computations oil the outputs of these to find texture boundaries. Previous models in this framework have been incompletely specified; our model is precisely stated and applicable to arbitrary grey scale textures. We claim that the responses of two types of mechanisms are necessary and sufficient: (a) center-surronud mechanisms of various widths. and (b) oriented tnechanisius of various widths and ori- entations which are even-symmetric about their axes. Simulation data oil a number of texture pairs is presented.

articleTitle: Spatial Light Modulators For Signal Processing Systems
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: The basic functions and operating modes of spatial light modulators that might be needed in signal processors and computer interconnections are reviewed, and brief descriptions given of major recent developments and their motivations.

articleTitle: Exploitation Of Parallelism In Vlsi Array Testing
publicationTitle: Twenty-Second Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
abstract: A systematic procedure for testing of VLSI reconfigurable arrays is proposed. The system is divided into three layers. Layer I includes configuration control circuit and busses to broadcast configuration information. Layer II covers the interconnection network and layer III contains the rest of the array including cell functional units. Testing (fault location) is performed from the lowest layer to the highest layer. Only the fault-free parts identified are used in the subsequent layer testing. Due to this separation, parallelism in testing has been exploited considerably. The algorithm can be realized with very low hardware overhead.
